messages:
sam-sales: Hey team — FinServX POC hit a wall. Their infra sits behind a corporate proxy + MITM and our JS & Python SDK calls are intermittently 502/504 and a handful of 429s. Can eng help triage? They also dropped the security questionnaire and a pricing Q.

alex-eng: On it. Can you paste a minimal failing curl or client log? 502/504 usually proxy + keepalive or chunking mismatch. 429 could be upstream rate-limiting or client retry storm.

maria-solutions: For pricing Q — they want an estimate for 200k tokens/month + 10k embedding units and Dedicated eval. I can draft ranges but will confirm with pricing ops after we scope retries/overage.

sam-sales: Log snippet from their Python client (redwood-python v0.9):
```
requests.exceptions.ReadTimeout: HTTPSConnectionPool(host='api.redwood.ai', port=443): Read timed out. (read timeout=30)
HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway\nUpstream: CONNECT_ERROR\n```
Also TS client shows `net::ERR_CONNECTION_RESET` when routed through their proxy appliance. They're using an explicit corporate proxy (proxy.company:8080) with TLS interception cert installed.

lee-eng: Two quick checks: (1) Are they setting HTTP_PROXY/HTTPS_PROXY in the environment or passing proxy config to the SDK? (2) Do their proxy logs show CONNECT being allowed to api.redwood.ai:443 or are CONNECTs proxied and re-signed?

sam-sales: They set env vars but still see resets. I asked them to share proxy logs; they said it rewrites re-used connections and kills long-lived sockets.

alex-eng: Sounds like connection reuse is tripping the proxy. Short-term workaround: disable HTTP keepalive / use short-lived connections and increase client timeout + enable exponential backoff. For Python requests session, set `session.trust_env = False` then configure proxies explicitly and `session.mount('https://', HTTPAdapter(pool_connections=0, pool_maxsize=1))` to avoid pooling. For TS/node, set `agent: false` or `keepAlive: false` on the http(s) agent.

lee-eng: Also add client-side rate limiting + jittered retries to avoid 429 storm. Our SDK config supports: `{ timeoutMs: 60000, maxRetries: 5, retryBackoffMs: 300 }` in TS and Python `client = RedwoodClient(timeout=60, max_retries=5, backoff_factor=0.3)`. If they still see 502s, suggest routing through a tunnel (eg. corporate proxy -> outbound bastion that does native TLS passthrough) so CONNECT isn't terminated.

maria-solutions: I'm capturing that and will update the SOW. For dedicated eval, rough pricing: hosted usage estimate $X-$Y/month for 200k tokens (I'll confirm). Also raised security Qs: data residency, audit logs, and KMS integration. @ingrid-security can you cover quick answers for the questionnaire?

ingrid-security: Quick answers: we support customer-managed KMS for Private/Dedicated, audit logs retained per contract (we have 90/180/365 options), and we can provide SOC2 Type 2 + ISO27001 attestation. For the questionnaire, ask them to flag items they need evidence for; I'll attach the cert bundle.

sam-sales: Thanks. Back to the integration — I pushed a small repro repo link to them: https://git.company/repro/redwood-proxy-poc (they can run tests).

deploy-bot: deploy status: :white_check_mark: production-agent v1.3.7 rolled out 03/11 09:12 UTC — no known regressions affecting connection handling.

alex-eng: Can you have them run two quick repro commands from behind their proxy and paste results?

1) curl through proxy with verbose:
```
curl -v -x http://proxy.company:8080 https://api.redwood.ai/v1/health
```
2) small python sample to exercise streaming/generate (with env `HTTPS_PROXY=http://proxy.company:8080`):
```
from redwood import RedwoodClient
c = RedwoodClient(api_key='REDACTED', timeout=60, max_retries=3)
print(c.health())
```
If curl fails at CONNECT that implicates the proxy. If curl succeeds but SDK fails only on streaming, it's probably chunked transfer or keepalive.

sam-sales: They ran curl and got:
```
* Connected to proxy.company (10.2.3.4) port 8080 (#0)
* Establish HTTP proxy tunnel to api.redwood.ai:443
> CONNECT api.redwood.ai:443 HTTP/1.1\n> Host: api.redwood.ai:443\n< HTTP/1.1 200 Connection established\n* Proxy re-signing cert and forwarding TLS handshake
* TLSv1.3 (IN), TLS handshake, Client hello (1)
* TLSv1.3 (IN), TLS alert, close_notify (256)
* Connection #0 to host proxy.company left intact
curl: (56) OpenSSL SSL_read: SSL_ERROR_SYSCALL, errno 104
```
So proxy accepts CONNECT but TLS handshake aborts.

lee-eng: That confirms MITM. Two options: (A) They add our root CA used in the proxy to the client trust store (not ideal), (B) use a TLS passthrough/bastion so our cert stays intact, or (C) ensure proxy allows SNI passthrough for api.redwood.ai and doesn't re-sign. For short-term, try disabling ALPN/HTTP2 in client — proxies sometimes choke on HTTP/2 upgrade. In curl: `--http1.1` and in node set `forceHttp1: true` (or set ALPN to http/1.1).

alex-eng: Also capture SDK debug logs: set `REDWOOD_LOG=debug` in env for both clients and paste. That shows handshake/resume behavior and timing for retries.

sam-sales: They tried `curl --http1.1` and it progressed further, returned 200 from /v1/health but streaming generate still cuts out. They applied our Python adapter change to disable pooling and increased timeout to 90s — streaming now mostly works but occasionally a single chunk fails then client retries and succeeds.

maria-solutions: Good — can you capture token counts so I can firm the usage estimate? We need to know retry overhead.

sam-sales: Will ask. FinServX also asked if we support per-route long polling SLOs for streaming connections for Dedicated.

lee-eng: Yes, Dedicated can set per-route timeouts and connection lifetimes; we'll need to configure the serving runtime with `connection.max_idle_ms` and `stream.keepalive_ms`. I can send example config.

ingrid-security: One more note for the questionnaire: confirm that re-signed TLS by customer proxy is a customer-controlled risk — we can provide mitigation guidance but cannot bypass their corporate interception. Documenting acceptance is required for compliance.

sam-sales: Great. Next steps: (1) I'll get their proxy logs and full REDWOOD_LOG debug dump, (2) maria will update pricing with retry overhead margin, (3) ingrid will attach cert bundle and guidance, (4) lee/alex to provide Dedicated config example for stream SLOs.

alex-eng: Happy path summary to include in repro: disable keepalive/pooling in client, force HTTP/1.1, enable retry/backoff, bump timeout to 60–90s. If they need persistence, recommend an outbound NAT/bastion that does TLS passthrough.

sam-sales: Customer confirms streaming stable after client tweaks. Marking this as resolved for now — will re-open if proxy change occurs. :thumbsup:

maria-solutions: I'll follow up with a pricing email and updated SOW this afternoon.

ingrid-security: I'll upload the cert bundle + SOC2 docs to the share and ping them.

sam-sales: Thanks everyone!
